title: Apple testing new HomePod features (AAPL)
text:
Apple testing new HomePod features (AAPL) Posted By: BusinessInsider July 24, 2018 This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence IoT Briefing subscribers hours before it appeared on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here .
Apple is testing several updates to the software for its HomePod smart speaker that would add key functionality for users, according to iGeneration reporting cited by Engadget . Specifically, Apple is testing a new voice calling feature for its smart speaker, along with the ability to set multiple simultaneous timers and a variant of its “Find my iPhone” feature. These new capabilities are currently undergoing internal beta testing, but there’s no apparent timeline for when they might make their way to the HomePod.
The HomePod got off to a rocky start after demonstrating strong early potential at its June 2017 unveiling. An early Business Insider Intelligence survey showed high consumer awareness of the product, as well as an excited audience.
But Apple initially planned to release the music-oriented smart speaker six months later, in time for the holiday season — and it failed to meet that target, delaying the device until February 2018 and squandering the initial wave of attention and excitement. Further hampering the smart speaker was a paucity of features and a lack of any third-party voice app development framework.
While there’s still no indication that Apple is looking to open the HomePod to third-party developers outside of very specific contexts, this news shows that the company is trying to address some of the HomePod’s issues. Calling, in particular, is a feature that both Amazon and Google — the leaders in the US smart speaker market — added to their smart speaker voice assistants early on to provide added functionality and let consumers start to rely on the devices for central functions like communication. For Apple, following this lead is a logical step for the HomePod and the electronics company as a whole, as much of its ecosystem revolves around the iPhone.
Adding key features like calling and multiple timers to the HomePod is smart, but it won’t be enough to push Apple to catch up to the likes of Amazon and Google in the smart speaker market. Apple’s device is presented to the market as speaker-first, with the smart side of things as a secondary consideration.
This strategy has worked for Sonos, which has developed a healthy business and numerous multi-product customers and is approaching an IPO. But Apple is a newcomer into this existing market, and it would need to either expand the market for high-end speakers — since consumers who want those have had ample opportunity to buy from other brands over the years — or offer features like AI integration that outperform the competition, which it hasn’t done.
HomePod sales so far have underwhelmed , and the purported features being tested aren’t likely to alter that trajectory on their own.
